case.summary: The case was triggered when the cardholder reported they did not make the flagged purchase, alongside 4 online purchases completed within 30 minutes that each stayed just under $500 to avoid an authorization threshold, originating from a new device profile (id_15). Decisive evidence included the customer's denial and the coordinated sub-$500 amounts across multiple device profiles. It was assumed the customer was telling the truth regarding the disputed charges. The verdict is fraud, and the actions of blocking the card, creating an internal case, filing a report, and escalating to an analyst follow directly from Fraud Policies R2, 3a, and R9 due to the customer denial, exposure exceeding $1,000, and an undocumented coordinated pattern.

sar.narrative: This report concerns customer C07297, card C07297-K1. On 2016-11-21, 4 transaction(s) (3476602, 3476633, 3476665, 3476682) totalling $1,906.07 were identified as suspicious. The activity was conducted online, billed to region(s) 264, 476, with amounts of $478.95, $456.96, $488.04, $482.12. The 4 purchases were made within 30 minutes and each was just under $500, indicating amounts deliberately sized to stay below a $500 authorization threshold. They came from 2 device profile(s): Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080; iOS Device | iOS 11.2.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2208x1242. Supporting detail: Flagged transaction came from a device marked New for this account (id_15). The cardholder reported the transaction as unauthorized. The activity is suspicious because it is inconsistent with the cardholder's established behaviour and matches a coordinated pattern not covered by the bank's documented typologies, as in prior confirmed cases CC-3748, CC-3841. Recommended actions: BLOCK_CARD, CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST. Total suspicious amount: $1,906.07.
